name: POST /api/leads/:id/first-response - Record the first human response and stop the SLA clock
description: Records a valid human first response against a lead, which STOPS its response clock and logs the measured response time for analysis. A command against an existing lead rather than the creation of a new resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). response_seconds is measured from the lead's created_at - the moment the prospect submitted - NOT from assigned_at: the prospect has been waiting since arrival, and measuring from assignment would let a lead sit unrouted for an hour and still report a fast response. state reports the outcome the ProjexCloud sdk-sla monitor computed: met when the response landed before sla_due_at, breached when it did not. When the gateway is unconfigured the handler falls back to a local wall-clock comparison and reports clock_source local_wallclock, so the field always tells a reader WHICH clock produced the verdict - the business-calendar clock only sdk-sla holds, or LeadFlow's plain wall-clock. monitor_delivered reports whether the observation reached sdk-sla; a false value means the local projection is authoritative for now and the reconciliation sweep (POST /api/sla/evaluate) will re-assert it. IDEMPOTENT: a lead whose clock has already been stopped answers 200 with already_recorded:true and the ORIGINAL first_response_at unchanged - a retry after a timeout must never overwrite the real response time with a later one, which would silently turn a breach into a pass. A lead with no owner and no sla_due_at can still record a response: the response genuinely happened, so it is logged with target_minutes null and no breach verdict rather than rejected. QA: depends on register (which creates the user named as responded_by_user_id), login, and a captured lead - intake auto-routing means that lead already has a running clock.

transitions.notes: The monitoring sweep moves a lead to at_risk once at least 80 percent of its response window has elapsed with no first response. Advisory only - no column changes, so the escalation ladder can act before a breach rather than after.
The sweep sets leads.sla_breached and sla_breach_reason no_response_in_window once sla_due_at has passed with first_response_at still null.
Sets first_response_at, which stops the clock, and writes the measured response time to sla_metrics. met means the response landed before sla_due_at.
A response inside the window still counts as met - at_risk is a warning, not a penalty.

A response after sla_due_at stops the clock but does NOT clear the breach. sla_breach_reason becomes responded_after_due and the observation is logged so the late response time is still available for analysis. A breach is a historical fact and is never erased by acting late.

testCases.name: Record a first response inside the window
Reject a lead id that is not a UUID

errorCases.when: the id path parameter is not a well-formed UUID (checked before the query so a malformed id answers 400 rather than causing Postgres to raise an invalid-input error that would surface as a 500), channel is absent or not one of the six response channels, note is over 500 characters, or responded_by_user_id is present but not a UUID
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no lead exists with the supplied id, or responded_by_user_id is a well-formed UUID that no user holds
